definition: Engineering mathematics applies mathematical methods to modeling, analysis and design in engineering.
example: An engineer uses differential equations to predict a suspension system's motion.

definition: Engineering statics studies the forces and moments on objects in equilibrium.
example: A structural engineer calculates the reactions at both supports of a beam.

definition: Engineering statistics applies probability and statistical inference to engineering data and decisions.
example: A reliability engineer estimates uncertainty in a component's average lifetime.

definition: An eNodeB is the LTE base station that manages radio communications between mobile devices and the core network.
example: An eNodeB allocates radio resources to phones in its cell.

definition: Environmental anthropology studies how human cultures and communities interact with and understand their environments.
example: A researcher studies how fishing practices reflect local knowledge of a river.

definition: Environmental finance examines how financial instruments, investment and risk management address environmental goals or impacts.
example: An analyst compares financing structures for restoring a watershed.

definition: Environmental, social and governance factors describe three groups of nonfinancial considerations used to evaluate organizations and investments.
example: A portfolio review considers emissions, workforce policies and board oversight.

definition: Equities are ownership interests in companies, commonly held as shares of stock.
example: A fund holds shares in several public companies as part of its equity allocation.

definition: Erikson's theory divides psychosocial development into eight life stages, each organized around a characteristic conflict.
example: A developmental psychology class discusses identity versus role confusion in adolescence.

definition: Ethical AI addresses how AI systems can be developed and used in ways that respect people and reduce harm.
example: A team evaluates whether an automated tool systematically disadvantages one user group.

definition: Etiology is the origin or cause of a disease or condition, or the study of those causes.
example: An epidemiologist investigates whether several cases share the same source.

definition: Excess return is the difference between an investment's return and a specified reference return.
example: A portfolio gaining 7 percent shows a 2-percentage-point excess return over a benchmark gaining 5 percent.
sense_note: The comparator can be a benchmark, risk-free rate or another specified reference.

definition: Expectancy theory explains motivation in terms of beliefs about whether effort leads to performance, performance to outcomes, and those outcomes are valued.
example: An employee is more willing to take on a difficult assignment when success seems attainable and the reward worthwhile.

definition: The Extended Parallel Process Model predicts responses to fear appeals from perceived threat and perceived ability to respond effectively.
example: A researcher compares whether a flood warning encourages preparation or leads recipients to tune out.

definition: Extended reality is an umbrella term for technologies that combine or substitute digital experiences for aspects of the physical world.
example: A training program combines augmented-reality instructions with a virtual-reality practice environment.

definition: An extended validation certificate is a public-key certificate issued after a certificate authority performs prescribed checks on an organization's identity.
example: A company seeks extended validation to have its legal identity vetted during certificate issuance.
sense_note: Browser presentation varies; it does not establish that the site is safe.

definition: Eye surgery comprises operations on the eye or its supporting structures to treat disease, injury or visual problems.
example: An ophthalmologist replaces a clouded lens during cataract surgery.

definition: Factoring is the sale of accounts receivable to a third party, commonly to receive cash before invoices come due.
example: A distributor sells unpaid invoices to a factor rather than waiting for customer payments.

definition: Family and consumer sciences studies everyday decisions about resources, well-being and relationships in households and communities.
example: A class teaches families to plan a food budget around nutrition and cost.

definition: Family ministry is organized religious work that supports families in their relationships, spiritual life and participation in a faith community.
example: A congregation offers a parenting discussion group through its family ministry.

definition: Family systems theory understands families as interdependent systems in which members' behavior and relationships influence one another.
example: A counselor examines how one person's stress changes patterns of communication across the household.

definition: Feminist theory includes frameworks for examining how gendered power and inequality shape social institutions and lived experience.
example: A researcher analyzes how assumptions about caregiving shape workplace promotion practices.

definition: Fibre Channel is a high-speed networking technology used chiefly to connect servers to shared storage.
example: A data center uses Fibre Channel to connect database servers to a storage array.

definition: A field-programmable gate array is a chip whose digital logic circuitry can be configured after manufacture.
example: An engineer configures an FPGA to filter multiple signal channels in parallel.

definition: A file control block is a data structure that holds the metadata an operating system uses to manage a file.
example: A system consults a file control block to locate stored file data.
sense_note: The specific fields and purpose differ across operating systems.

definition: Final expense insurance is life insurance marketed to help beneficiaries cover funeral and other end-of-life costs.
example: A beneficiary uses the policy proceeds toward a funeral bill.

definition: Financial privacy concerns control over who can collect, use and disclose information about a person's finances.
example: A banking app asks permission before sharing transaction history with a budgeting service.

definition: Flexible Single Master Operations are Active Directory roles that assign specific directory-wide or domain-wide operations to designated domain controllers.
example: An administrator checks which domain controller holds the schema master role before a schema change.

definition: Floating-point arithmetic performs calculations on finite-precision numbers represented with a significand and exponent.
example: A programmer uses a tolerance when comparing the results of two approximate calculations.

definition: Fluid statics studies pressure and forces in liquids and gases at rest.
example: An engineer calculates how water pressure increases with depth along a stationary tank wall.

definition: Folk music includes musical traditions passed through communities and the styles that draw on those traditions.
example: Participants learn a local dance tune by playing it together at gatherings.

definition: Food economics studies how prices, policies and incentives shape food production, distribution and consumption.
example: An economist examines how rising transport costs affect grocery prices.

definition: Food microbiology studies microorganisms that affect how foods ferment, spoil or transmit illness.
example: A food scientist studies the cultures that give yogurt its texture and acidity.

definition: Food process engineering applies engineering principles to design and control operations that transform or preserve foods.
example: An engineer sizes a heat exchanger for a beverage production line.

definition: Food safety comprises practices and controls that prevent food from harming consumers.
example: A cafeteria keeps raw ingredients separate from prepared salads.

definition: Food science studies the composition, properties and behavior of foods during production, storage and use.
example: A team investigates why a sauce separates during refrigerated storage.

definition: Forced draft systems use a fan or blower to push air into equipment that needs controlled airflow.
example: A boiler uses a forced draft fan to supply air for combustion.

definition: Forensic dentistry applies dental expertise to questions of identification and legal evidence.
example: A specialist compares dental records with available dental evidence to help identify remains.

definition: Forklift safety concerns practices that reduce collisions, tip-overs and other injuries during forklift operation.
example: A warehouse uses separate travel lanes for pedestrians and forklifts.

definition: A fuel cell converts chemical energy into electricity through an electrochemical reaction while reactants are supplied.
example: A stationary fuel cell supplies backup electricity to a facility.
